summary: notification-service's near-daily OOMKills (exit 137) are caused by the unbounded in-memory TemplateCache introduced in v3.8.0 (2026-03-21T00:00Z), which never evicts and grows monotonically (~50k -> ~190-197k entries) within each ~22-23h cycle until old-gen heap saturates and the kubelet kills the pod. Confidence is medium (0.70, capped by the Critic): the cache size resets exactly at each restart in lockstep with the container memory sawtooth, and the GC-exhaustion-then-exit-137 signature recurs on 03-21/03-22/03-23 independent of the 03-23 Kafka maintenance. The reporter's Kafka-replay theory and the alternative config/upstream/limit-reduction hypotheses are actively contradicted by verified findings (no replay/rebalance/deserialization errors; lag spikes coincide with rather than precede the OOM; no config change touching notification-service limits). Two residuals keep this short of certainty: whether OOMs predate the deploy is unrecoverable (telemetry starts 03-20), and byte-level heap attribution to the cache is unmeasurable, so the cache's majority-of-heap share rests on correlation with mild counter-evidence in the non-constant entry-count/memory ratio.

ranked_hypotheses.title: notification-service v3.8.0's unbounded in-memory TemplateCache leaks heap and OOMs the pod
ranked_hypotheses.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 (2026-03-21T00:00Z) added an in-memory TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) with no eviction bound. Distinct keys are retained indefinitely, so heap grows steadily with traffic; over ~22h the heap crosses the container limit, producing escalating old-gen full GCs, and the kubelet OOMKills the pod (exit 137). The restart clears the cache, memory drops back to ~46-48%, and the cycle repeats roughly daily. The reported ~25min email delay and the consumer-lag spike are consequences of the restart/backlog drain, not its cause.

causal_chain.claim: Deployment v3.8.0 adds an unbounded in-memory TemplateCache (no eviction, evictions=0 on every log line) at 2026-03-21T00:00Z.
Cache entry count grows monotonically within each cycle, ~9k -> ~190-197k entries, never evicting.
Container memory_pct ramps steadily and linearly (~4-5%/2h) from a ~46-48% post-restart floor to 93-98% over ~22-24h (sawtooth), matching the cache refill window.
Heap saturation produces escalating old-gen full-GC WARNs, ending in a kubelet OOMKill (exit 137).
Memory and cache size reset together at each restart, then recur ~every 23h across 03-21/03-22/03-23.
The restart causes a transient consumer-lag spike and ~25min email delay while the backlog drains; lag returns to baseline within ~30min.
Only notification-service shows the sawtooth; auth/order/settlement (sharing cluster/Kafka consumer infra) stay flat at ~49-60% with zero restarts, excluding a cluster/infra-wide cause.

assumptions: TemplateCache entries are the dominant contributor to live heap. F14/F15/F34 show the cache count and memory reset in lockstep, but this is correlation: F31/F32/F35 confirm no per-class byte metric, no heap-region metric and no cache-bytes field exist, so allocation attribution was never measurable. F33/F36 further show the entry-count-to-memory ratio is not constant (03-21: 196650 entries at ~92.9%; 03-22: 196650 at ~94.4-94.7%; 03-23: only 188100 at ~94.5%), which is mild evidence that not all peak memory is cache-proportional.

The OOM episodes began at/after the 03-21 deployment. Telemetry only starts 2026-03-20T00:00Z and 03-01..03-19 is unrecoverable (F25/F30), so this rests on the single pre-deploy baseline day 03-20 being flat at ~48% mean with zero restarts (F28/F29) and the first observable exit-137 being 03-21T22:59:50Z (F26).

The post-restart cache floor differs (9000 entries after the 03-23 OOM vs ~49-51k mid-cycle floors) yet memory floors stay ~46-48%; this discrepancy is unexplained by any available metric and is the residual opening for a non-cache contributor.
Traffic carries enough distinct template+locale+userSegment keys to grow the cache to ~190-200k entries per ~22h cycle.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Chronic pre-existing memory growth / underprovisioned heap, with the cache as accelerator not origin
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A pre-existing slow memory growth or an underprovisioned heap limit (independent of v3.8.0) gradually exhausts notification-service's headroom; the v3.8.0 TemplateCache adds pressure or accelerates the ramp but is not the origin. The fix would be raising the limit or fixing the pre-existing leak, not reverting the cache.

causal_chain.claim: Steady-state memory grows over time regardless of the cache (pre-existing leak or traffic outgrowing the provisioned limit).
Provisioned heap headroom is exhausted after ~22h, producing the near-daily OOM cycle.

assumptions: Some non-cache allocation leaks or the limit is simply too low for steady load — no such source is identified anywhere in telemetry.
The single pre-03-20 baseline day (F28/F29) is not representative and a longer pre-deploy window could reveal prior OOMs — unrecoverable (F25/F30).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Weakened but not formally falsified, per the critic. No independent non-cache leak is evidenced, while the cache size and the memory sawtooth reset together at every restart (F14/F15/F34), the one pre-deploy baseline day is flat at ~48% with zero restarts (F28/F29), and post-restart the heap resumes climbing in lockstep with cache refill (F9). The non-constant count/bytes-per-entry ratio (F33/F36) is the only residual support, and it does not identify an alternative source. Retained rejected at low confidence because the onset discriminator is unobtainable (F25/F30).

ranked_hypotheses.title: A memory-limit/quota reduction (config change) narrowed headroom, making a normal cache footprint OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A config change reduced notification-service's container memory limit or resource quota, so an otherwise-acceptable memory footprint (e.g. the template cache) now exceeds the limit and OOMs. Fix would be restoring the limit.

causal_chain.claim: A config change lowered the memory limit/quota for notification-service.
Normal memory usage then exceeds the reduced limit, triggering OOMKill.

assumptions: Such a config change exists but was not returned by the API (the gap explicitly flags this cannot be fully ruled out because get_config_changes may be scoped).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The only config change in the entire window is cfg-2410 (Kafka retention, F2); an explicit search found no change touching notification-service memory limits/quotas/consumer settings (F4). A limit reduction would create an abrupt new ceiling, not a linear ~22h ramp from ~48% to ~95% (F8, F9), and the recurring near-daily pattern starting 03-21 (F7) indicates a growing footprint. Retained at low confidence only because the config API may not have surfaced such a change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: An upstream producer or the external email-provider degraded, causing message accumulation in notification-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A producer up the chain or the external email-provider slowed or changed, slowing notification-service's processing so messages accumulate in memory (in-flight buffer or retry-driven cache growth) until OOM. Fix would be at the upstream producer or email-provider.

causal_chain.claim: An upstream producer or the email-provider slowed or changed behavior.
notification-service accumulates in-flight/retry messages, raising memory.

assumptions: The un-enumerated upstream producers actually changed behavior — none are recorded in the graph (F3 upstream edges empty).
In-flight accumulation rather than the cache is the memory consumer — contradicted by F14/F15/F34 showing cache size tracks memory and resets with each OOM.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No upstream producers are recorded in the dependency graph (F3); the only neighbor is email-provider with has_telemetry=false and no degradation evidence. The memory sawtooth tracks the internal TemplateCache (F14/F15/F34), not inbound volume; OOMs recur near-daily including days before any external change (F7); and lag spikes coincide with restarts (F11/F12), consistent with post-restart drain, not upstream backlog. Mechanism mismatch.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance (retention reduction) triggered a consumer replay that notification-service buffered in memory
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reporter's hypothesis: the 2026-03-23T18:00Z Kafka config change cfg-2410 (log.retention.ms 7d->3d) plus broker maintenance caused a consumer-group rebalance/replay; notification-service's consumer buffered the replayed backlog in memory and OOMKilled ~2h20m later at 19:59Z. Fix would be consumer batching/backpressure tuning or staggering maintenance.

causal_chain.claim: Kafka maintenance reduces retention at 2026-03-23T18:00Z via cfg-2410.
Maintenance/rebalance triggers a consumer replay of a large backlog.
notification-service consumer buffers replayed messages in memory.
Memory blows up abruptly and OOMKills the pod ~2h20m later.

assumptions: A replay actually occurred on 2026-03-23 — no replay/rebalance is logged (F17 shows none).
The memory rise would have been abrupt rather than a ~22h steady ramp (F8/F9).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Closed by multiple verified findings: OOMs occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 with no Kafka maintenance (F7, F26); memory climbs steadily for ~22h and the ramp predates the 18:00Z change (F8, F16); Kafka logged no replay/rebalance/error activity around the maintenance (F17); the 03-21 OOM shows no deserialization/replay errors (F13, F18); and the lag spike is simultaneous with the OOM, indicating consequence rather than trigger (F11, F12). Residual caveat: the deserialization-error search across the full window was never executed (budget), so 'zero replay errors' is inferred from the 03-21/03-23 log sets — not blocking given timing and absence of any rebalance event.

facts.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 was deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z with 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment), status live, not rolled back; it is one of only two deployments in the 03-16..03-23 window.

notification-service was OOMKilled exactly 3 times this week, all near ~20:00Z: 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, exit code 137, container notification-service-7d9f; intervals are ~23h apart (near-daily).

Container memory grows steadily and linearly (~4-5% per 2h) from a ~46-48% post-restart floor to ~95-98% over ~22h before each OOM, forming a sawtooth rather than an abrupt spike, and resets sharply at each restart.

TemplateCache never evicts: every 'TemplateCache stats' line reports evictions=0, and the entry count grows monotonically within each cycle (03-21: 51750->103500->155250->196650; 03-22: 51750->103500->155250->196650; 03-23: 49500->99000->148500->188100), resetting only at the restart (9000 entries after the 03-23 OOM).

Each OOM is preceded by escalating old-gen full-GC WARNs ('heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took Nms') terminating in the exit-137 OOMKilled: 03-21 from 21:37:01Z (4317ms) to 22:41:43Z (7457ms) before the 22:59:50Z kill; 03-23 from 18:34:46Z (4152ms) to 19:49:28Z (6488ms) before 19:59:21Z, with no deserialization/replay/consumer errors around either.

Consumer lag is flat (~50-70 msgs) in steady state but spikes to avg/max 2273/17161 (03-21T22:00), 790/17611 (03-22T20:00) and 810/18137 (03-23T18:00); 10-min data pins the 03-23 spike to 19:50-20:10Z, simultaneous with the 19:59:21Z OOM and the memory reset, so lag is a consequence of restart/backlog drain rather than a trigger.

The only config change in the window is cfg-2410 (kafka log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000, 7d -> 3d) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z, ~2h20m before the reported OOM; no config change touching notification-service memory limits, quotas, consumer settings, batch sizes or max.poll.records was returned.

Kafka logs show no replay/rebalance/error activity around the maintenance or the OOM: the only non-heartbeat entries are the cfg-2410 config-change line at 18:00:24Z and benign segment rolls; all other entries are 'group coordinator heartbeat ok'.
The memory ramp precedes the Kafka maintenance: on 03-21 memory climbed from avg 72.97% at 12:00Z to 95.83%/max 96.95% at 22:00Z, and OOMs occurred on 03-21 and 03-22, before any Kafka maintenance.

Only notification-service shows this pattern: auth-service (52.01% mean, max 59.27%, restarts 0), settlement-service (~49-50.5%, no >90%) and order-service (~59-60.8%, restarts 0) are all flat with no sawtooth, and auth-service emits none of the >90% old-gen / OOMKilled WARN signature, excluding an infra/node-wide cause.

The only pre-deploy baseline day available, 2026-03-20, shows flat memory around ~48% mean (min 42.73, max 54.77) with zero restarts and no upward ramp, and the first observable OOMKilled (exit 137) is 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z.
notification-service telemetry begins only at 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z; all log and metric queries for 2026-03-01..2026-03-19 returned empty, so any pre-03-20 OOM history is unrecoverable.

The TemplateCache count near peak is not identical across cycles and the entry-count-to-memory ratio is not constant: 03-21 reached 196650 entries at ~92.9%, 03-22 196650 at ~94.4-94.7%, but 03-23 reached only 188100 entries when memory was already 93.86-94.47%, implying a higher bytes-per-entry on 03-23.

No heap/region/class-histogram telemetry exists for notification-service: the heap_old_gen_bytes metric is not_found, available_metrics are exactly ['consumer_lag','cpu_pct','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','request_rate','restarts'], the TemplateCache log line carries entry count only ('size=<n> entries, evictions=<n>'), and GC WARNs report only percentage over 90 plus GC duration — so no byte-level attribution of live heap to the cache is possible.

assumptions: Assumption: TemplateCache entries are the dominant contributor to live heap. F14/F15/F34 show cache count and memory reset in lockstep, but this is correlation, not measured attribution — F31/F32/F35 confirm there is no per-class byte metric, no heap-region metric and no cache-bytes field, so allocation attribution was never measurable. F33/F36 (non-constant entry-count-to-memory ratio: 03-21 196650 entries at ~92.9%; 03-22 196650 at ~94.4-94.7%; 03-23 only 188100 at ~94.5%) is mild evidence not all peak memory is cache-proportional.

Assumption: The OOM episodes began at/after the 03-21 deployment. Because telemetry only starts 2026-03-20T00:00Z and 03-01..03-19 is unrecoverable (F25/F30), this rests on the single pre-deploy baseline day 03-20 being flat at ~48% with zero restarts (F28/F29) and the first observable exit-137 being 03-21T22:59:50Z (F26).

Assumption: The post-restart cache floor differs (9000 entries after the 03-23 OOM vs ~49-51k mid-cycle floors) while memory floors stay ~46-48%; this discrepancy is unexplained by any available metric and is the residual opening for a non-cache contributor (H5).

Assumption: Traffic carries enough distinct template+locale+userSegment keys to grow the cache to ~190-200k entries per ~22h cycle (inferred from observed growth curves, not from a traffic-cardinality measurement).

Assumption: The reported ~25 min email delay and consumer-lag spike are consequences of the restart/backlog drain rather than the cause; the delay window itself was not verified from logs or metrics (tool budget exhausted).

Assumption: auth-service, settlement-service and order-service run on the same node/cluster and share Kafka consumer infrastructure; service selection was based on shared Kafka infrastructure and comparable memory_pct, and node topology was not independently verified.

timeline.event: Earliest available notification-service telemetry; all queries for 2026-03-01..2026-03-19 return no data, so earlier history is unavailable.
Pre-deploy baseline day: memory_pct flat at ~48% mean (max 54.77%) with restarts=0 all day; no sawtooth.
notification-service v3.8.0 deployed ('Add in-memory template cache for email rendering'), status live, not rolled back.
First >90% old-gen full-GC WARN of the first cycle (full GC 4317ms), escalating to 7457ms at 22:41:43Z.
First observable OOMKilled (exit 137) of notification-service pod notification-service-7d9f; TemplateCache had reached 196650 entries at 21:51:13Z with memory ~92.9%.
Second cycle: TemplateCache at 196650 entries with memory ~94.4-94.7% (20:25-20:45Z), immediately preceding the next OOM.
Second near-daily OOMKilled (exit 137); cache and memory reset at the restart.
Kafka config change cfg-2410 applied (log.retention.ms 7d -> 3d) as 'Kafka maintenance'; the only config change in the window.
Kafka logs record only the cfg-2410 config change and benign segment rolls; no replay, rebalance or error activity.
Third cycle's >90% old-gen full-GC WARN series begins (4152ms), escalating to 6488ms at 19:49:28Z; memory at 18:45-18:54Z was already 93.86-94.47% with 188100 cached entries.
Consumer lag spikes to avg 9089->12294, max 18137 over 19:50-20:10Z, i.e. simultaneous with, not preceding, the OOM.
Third OOMKilled (exit 137) of notification-service-7d9f; memory drops sharply to ~46.45% by 20:00Z and TemplateCache resets to 9000 entries by 21:00Z.
INC-004 reported (SEV-3): third OOM restart this week, ~25 min email delay, suspected Kafka-replay cause.
Post-restart, memory resumes climbing (46.45% at 20:00Z -> 55.48% at 23:50Z), beginning the next cycle.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: roll back / disable the TemplateCache — roll notification-service back from v3.8.0 (deployment 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', 2026-03-21T00:00Z) to the pre-cache build, or feature-flag off the cache and render templates without caching. This removes the unbounded structure that grows to ~190-197k entries with evictions=0 and is the only object whose size resets in lockstep with the memory sawtooth at every restart.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the accepted root cause; the cache never evicts (F14/F34) and its resets coincide exactly with memory resets at each OOM (F9/F15), so removing it stops the leak. It is the only change in the deployment window (F1).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate safety net: raise notification-service's container memory limit / add headroom and ensure the readiness/liveness probes and restart policy drain consumer lag cleanly, so another saturation does not repeat the ~25 min email delay reported here. Do NOT treat this as the fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: The container saturates to 95-98% before each exit-137 kill and lag then spikes to max ~18k while the backlog drains (F8/F11/F12). Headroom buys time but the ~22h linear ramp shows the leak continues regardless (F8/F9).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate (validate the acceptance): after the rollback, confirm the memory_pct series is flat (~48-55%) with restarts=0 and TemplateCache stats no longer grow over at least one full 24h cycle; also confirm consumer lag returns to the ~50-70 msg steady state. If memory still ramps without the cache, the residual H5 (non-cache contributor, supported by the non-constant entry-count/memory ratio F33/F36) must be escalated and investigated as a second source.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the cheapest discriminating test between H1 and the rejected-but-unfalsified H5, and it directly falsifies or confirms the accepted mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: replace the unbounded ConcurrentHashMap with a size-bounded/weighted cache (LRU or size-based eviction, e.g. bounded max entries or memory-based limit) and add cache metrics exposing entry count AND estimated bytes plus an eviction counter, so eviction is observable and the leak budget is measurable.
recommended_actions.rationale: evictions=0 on every line and no byte field is the structural defect (F14/F32); the count-only metric is exactly what made byte attribution impossible (F31/F32/F35).

recommended_actions.action: Short term: add capacity/leak guardrails around the template+locale+userSegment key space (e.g. bound the userSegment cardinality or hash it) and alert on TemplateCache growth rate and on 'heap usage over 90 (old gen)' before it reaches 95%, tying an alert to the recurring ~22-23h cycle so it is caught hours ahead of an OOM rather than after a restart.
recommended_actions.rationale: The key space grows with traffic and distinct keys are retained indefinitely (F1/F34); the escalation is gradual and detectable — 10 GC WARNs spread over 1.5h precede each kill (F10/F18).

recommended_actions.action: Long term: provision heap/region/class-byte observability (or periodic heap dumps/class histograms) for notification-service so live-heap attribution can be measured rather than inferred, and bake a memory-budget check into the deployment pipeline for cache-like data structures.
recommended_actions.rationale: No heap_old_gen_bytes metric exists and available_metrics contain only memory_pct with no byte denominator, so cache-vs-non-cache attribution was permanently unmeasurable and remains the residual uncertainty (F31/F32/F35/F36).

recommended_actions.action: Long term: for the reported Kafka-maintenance incident class, keep maintenance and consumer-tuning actions separate and pre-verify that a retention/rebalance change does not trigger replay buffering; note the historical precedents HIST-104/HIST-112 (broker-rebalance lag/delayed-email storms) do NOT document OOMKilled and are not the mechanism here.
recommended_actions.rationale: Kafka logged no replay/rebalance and the 03-21/03-22 OOMs predate the maintenance, so the maintenance theory (H2) is contradicted (F7/F17/F18); documenting this avoids re-misattributing future incidents.

data_gaps: Notification-service telemetry begins only at 2026-03-20T00:00Z; 2026-03-01..2026-03-19 is unrecoverable (F25/F30), so whether any OOM or >90% old-gen GC WARN occurred before the 2026-03-21 deployment — the decisive H1-vs-H5 onset discriminator — cannot be answered.

No heap/region/class-histogram metric and no cache-bytes field exist (heap_old_gen_bytes is not_found; TemplateCache logs entry count only; GC WARNs report only '% over 90'), so whether TemplateCache holds the majority of live heap bytes at peak versus a co-resident non-cache allocation is unmeasurable (F31/F32/F35/F36).

No config-change API result beyond cfg-2410 was returned, so it cannot be confirmed whether notification-service memory limits, quotas, max.poll.records, batch or fetch settings were ever changed; absence may reflect API scope (F2/F4).

The dependency graph returned no upstream producers (upstream edges empty; only kafka queue-consume and email-provider external with has_telemetry=false), so the topics/producers feeding the consumer group are not enumerated and the email-provider's health could not be checked.

The reported ~25 min email-delivery delay was not verified from logs or metrics, and email-service is not a valid service (known service is email-provider); the delay timing therefore rests on the incident description.

A deserialization/replay-error log search over the full 03-16..03-23 window was never executed (tool budget), so 'zero replay errors' is inferred from the 03-21/03-23 log sets and the absence of any Kafka rebalance event (F13/F17/F18).

A re-verification of Kafka consumer lag at 1-minute resolution around the 18:00Z maintenance was not executed, so the lag-spike onset relative to the maintenance rests on the coarser buckets and the 19:50-20:10Z zoom (F11/F12).

settlement-service's restarts metric query failed (backend 503) and its WARN log search for 'old gen'/'OOMKilled' was never run, so its exclusion from the blast radius rests on flat memory_pct alone (F21).
Cluster/node topology was not queried, so the assumption that auth/settlement/order co-reside with notification-service is taken from the incident framing rather than a verified node assignment.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that notification-service OOMs or >90% old-gen GC events occurred BEFORE the 2026-03-21 v3.8.0 deployment (from a longer/recovered telemetry window) would shift support toward H5 (pre-existing leak / underprovisioned heap) and reduce the cache's causal role — this window is currently unrecoverable (F25/F30).

A heap-dump or class-histogram showing TemplateCache holds only a small fraction of live heap bytes at ~95% memory would falsify H1's mechanism and point to H5, a different non-cache leak (F31/F32/F36).
A surviving notification-service pod with TemplateCache disabled (feature flag off) that still ramps from ~48% to >90% over ~22h would falsify H1 and confirm H5.
A confirmed Kafka consumer replay/rebalance or deserialization-error storm temporally preceding an OOM (rather than simultaneous lag) would revive H2 (F17 currently shows none).
A record of a notification-service memory-limit/quota reduction or consumer-settings change narrowing headroom would revive H3 (F4 currently returns no such change, though API scope is unclear).

A correlation between an upstream producer's or email-provider's degradation and the memory ramp — rather than the cache fill — would revive H4 (currently no upstream producers are recorded and email-provider has no telemetry, F3).

A constant entry-count-to-memory ratio and constant post-restart cache floor across cycles would strengthen the cache-attribution; conversely, further divergence (e.g. the 9000 vs ~49-51k post-restart floor discrepancy) would strengthen the residual H5 opening (F15/F33/F36).

findings.statement: Across ALL services in 2026-03-16..2026-03-23 only two deployments occurred: notification-service v3.8.0 at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z ('Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment, status live, not rolled back) and auth-service v7.1.4 at 2026-03-22T13:00:00Z ('Patch release', bump jackson). No deployment on 2026-03-23.

The only config change in the whole window is cfg-2410: kafka log.retention.ms changed 604800000 -> 259200000 (7 days -> 3 days) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team, described as 'Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'. This is ~2h20m before the 20:20Z report time.

notification-service's dependency graph (both directions, depth 2) contains only two edges: notification-service -> kafka (kind queue-consume) and notification-service -> email-provider (kind external, has_telemetry false). kafka is marked shared=true (owner platform); notification-service is shared=false, owner growth, has_telemetry=true. The upstream-only query returned zero edges, so no upstream producer services are recorded in the graph.

No config change touching notification-service memory limits, resource quotas, consumer settings, batch sizes, or max.poll.records was returned for the window — cfg-2410 (Kafka retention) is the single entry. A search of historical notification/Kafka incidents for 'template cache memory growth email rendering' could not be run because the task tool-call budget was exhausted.

Historical precedent search found HIST-104 (2025-11-05, 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance', symptoms consumer lag spike + delayed emails, root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm') and HIST-112 (2026-02-03, 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment', settlement-service + kafka, 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'). Both are broker-maintenance/rebalance precedents with the same lag/delayed-email symptoms as INC-004, but neither documents an OOMKilled restart. Per tool guidance these are leads, not evidence about the current incident.

The two candidate change events precede the reported OOM by very different intervals: notification-service v3.8.0 (in-memory template cache) landed ~2.8 days before the 2026-03-23T20:20Z report, while the Kafka retention/mainenance change landed ~2h20m before it. A third OOM restart 'this week' is consistent with the cache deployment window, but the tool outputs contain no memory/restart timeline to confirm which change correlates with the restarts.

notification-service OOMKilled exactly 3 times this week, all at ~20:00Z: 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z — exit code 137, container notification-service-7d9f. Intervals are ~23h apart (near-daily), not tied to a single Kafka-maintenance event.

Memory grows steadily and linearly (~4-5% per 2h bucket) from a ~48% post-restart floor and climbs to ~95-98% over ~22h before each OOM — a sawtooth pattern, not an abrupt spike. Examples: 2026-03-21 00:00=48.23% -> 20:00=92.91% (then OOM reset to 50.33%); 2026-03-23 00:00=52.99% -> 18:00=95.05% (then reset to 48.33%). This is consistent with a slow leak.

The 10-min zoom of memory confirms the reset points: 2026-03-23 memory sat at 93-98% through 19:50 (max 98.44%) then dropped sharply to ~46.45% by 20:00Z, matching the 19:59:21Z OOM restart. After restart it resumes climbing (46.45% at 20:00 -> 55.48% at 23:50).

GC/heap pressure logs precede each near-OOM: on 2026-03-23, 10 WARN events 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took Nms' from 18:34:46Z (4152ms) escalating to 19:49:28Z (6488ms), ending in the 19:59:21Z OOM. Long, lengthening full-GC times point to a heap filling over time.

findings.statement: Consumer lag is flat (~50-70 msgs) during steady state but spikes to very high values in the hours bracketing each OOM: 2026-03-21T22:00 avg=2273/max=17161; 2026-03-22T20:00 avg=790/max=17611; 2026-03-23T18:00 avg=810/max=18137. Zoomed 10-min data pins the 2026-03-23 spike to 19:50-20:10 (avg 9089->12294, max 18137), i.e. lag spike coincides with the OOM, not the alleged Kafka maintenance.

The lag spike and OOM are effectively simultaneous (lag peak 19:50-20:10Z, OOM at 19:59:21Z, memory reset to 46% at 20:00Z), so the lag is more plausibly a consequence of the restart/backlog drain than an independent trigger; and lag always returns to ~50-70 msgs within ~30 min afterward.

The 2026-03-21 first OOM of the week: notification-service logs show escalating full-GC WARNs ('heap usage 8% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4317ms' at 21:37:01Z rising to 7457ms at 22:41:43Z) terminating in 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting' at 22:59:50Z. No deserialization/replay/consumer errors appear around it.

TemplateCache is unbounded and never evicts: every 'TemplateCache stats' line shows evictions=0, and size climbs in lockstep with memory (155250 at 2026-03-21T17:15Z and 196650 at 21:51:13Z just before the 22:59 OOM; 196650 just before the 2026-03-22 OOM), then drops to 9000 entries only right after the 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z OOM restart.

The TemplateCache size sawtooth resets exactly at each restart: 2026-03-21T17:15=155250 -> 21:51=196650 (OOM 22:59), then post-restart 03-22T04:45=51750; 03-22T16:15=155250 -> 20:51=196650 (OOM 21:59), then 03-23T03:30=49500; and 03-23T18:54=188100 (OOM 19:59), then 21:00=9000. This mirrors the memory sawtooth and is consistent with an unbounded cache, not a replay-driven spike.

Memory ramps steadily toward the limit with no abrupt spike at the maintenance: 2026-03-21 12:00Z avg=72.97% climbing monotonically to 22:00Z avg=95.83%/max=96.95%, then reset to 46.24% at 23:00Z (post-OOM). The ramp precedes the 2026-03-23T18:00Z Kafka retention change, ruling out the maintenance as the onset trigger.

Kafka shows no replay/rebalance/error activity around today's maintenance or OOM: its only non-heartbeat entries are 'config change cfg-2410 applied: log.retention.ms=259200000' at 18:00:24Z and benign segment rolls (e.g. 'log segment rolled for partition orders-11' at 20:28:31Z). All other entries are 'group coordinator heartbeat ok'. No replay storm or rebalance logged.

Today's 2026-03-23 OOM signature matches the prior two: 10 GC WARNs from 18:34:46Z ('full GC took 4152ms') escalating to 19:49:28Z ('full GC took 6488ms') then 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting' at 19:59:21Z. The escalation window (~1.5h) postdates the 18:00Z maintenance, but the identical pattern on 03-21/03-22 without any maintenance indicates replay/deserialization is not the trigger.

auth-service reports restarts=0 in every 3h bucket across 2026-03-21..2026-03-23 (summary min/max/mean all 0.0), so no OOMKilled/restart events for the service the deployment graph shows as the only other recently-deployed service (v7.1.4).

settlement-service memory_pct over 2026-03-21..2026-03-23 is flat: every 3h bucket avg ~49-50.5% (min 44.44%, max 56.06%, mean 49.92%), no sawtooth and no >90% values. settlement-service is another Kafka consumer (exposes consumer_lag) and does not share notification-service's pattern.

order-service memory_pct over 2026-03-21..2026-03-23 is flat: every 3h bucket avg ~59-60.8% (min 51.57%, max 66.74%, mean 59.99%), no sawtooth and no >90% values; and order-service restarts=0 in all buckets.

No auth-service WARN log entries matching 'old gen' or 'OOMKilled' were returned for 2026-03-21..2026-03-23 (total_matched=0, returned=0, truncated=false; data_range covers 2026-03-20..2026-03-23), so auth-service shows none of notification-service's >90% old-gen full-GC WARN signature.

Three independent services sharing the cluster/Kafka consumer infrastructure (auth, settlement, order) all show flat, sub-67% memory with zero restarts, while only notification-service shows the ~22-24h sawtooth to >90% old-gen and exit-137 OOMs; this exclusivity is consistent with a service-specific cause (H1) rather than a cluster/node/infra-wide memory problem.

notification-service telemetry begins only at 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z: log queries for 2026-03-01..2026-03-21 all returned 0 matches with data_range.start='2026-03-20T00:00:00Z', and memory_pct/restarts metric queries with start=2026-03-01/03-03 return their first point at 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z (total_points 289, missing_points 0). No data exists for 2026-03-01..2026-03-19.

In the earliest available window (2026-03-20..2026-03-23), the first OOMKilled/exit-137 restart for notification-service is at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z ('container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting'), preceded by an escalating full-GC WARN series starting 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z.

findings.statement: The earliest WARN of any kind in the available log window is 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z ('GC pause 253ms exceeded 200ms target'); the >90%-old-gen full-GC WARN signature first appears at 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z. But these are only the earliest within data that starts 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z, so they cannot establish a true first-ever occurrence.

The 'restarts' (cumulative count) metric is 0.0 for every bucket from 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z through 2026-03-20T23:55:00Z (min/max/mean all 0.0) — the pre-03-21 baseline day shows zero restarts, consistent with the pod being stable on 2026-03-20 before the deploy at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z.

On 2026-03-20 (pre-deploy day), memory_pct is flat around a ~48% mean (summary mean=48.06, min=42.73, max=54.77) with no upward ramp and a stable post-restart-like floor — no sign of the sawtooth climb that characterizes the post-deploy period.

Because notification-service logs and metrics both start at 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z, the requested 2026-03-01..2026-03-19 pre-deploy span is unrecoverable from this backend; the H1-vs-H5 question of whether v3.8.0 (deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z) was the first-ever OOM trigger cannot be answered from telemetry — the earliest observable OOMKilled (2026-03-21T22:59:50Z) is post-deploy and the ~2.8-day baseline window available (03-20 only) is pre-deploy but too short to bound 'first-ever'.

notification-service exposes no heap/region/class-histogram metric: a query for heap_old_gen_bytes failed with not_found, and available_metrics is exactly ['consumer_lag','cpu_pct','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','request_rate','restarts']. There is no metric giving absolute old-gen or per-class byte counts, and memory_pct is a bare percentage with no byte denominator, so a bytes-by-class heap breakdown cannot be assembled from metrics.

The TemplateCache log line contains entry count only, no byte/size-in-bytes field: the single pattern is 'TemplateCache stats: size=<n> entries, evictions=<n>' across all 14 INFO lines (e.g. size=196650 entries, evictions=0). This is the only cache-related telemetry, so TemplateCache bytes cannot be read directly.

Across the three OOM cycles the TemplateCache entry count near peak is NOT the same, and the entry-count-to-memory ratio is not constant: 03-21 reached 196650 entries (21:51Z) with memory ~92.9%; 03-22 reached 196650 entries (20:51Z) with memory ~94.4-94.7% (20:25-20:45Z); 03-23 reached only 188100 entries (18:54Z) yet memory was already 93.86% and 94.47% at 18:45Z. So the 03-23 cycle hit equal-or-higher memory with ~8500 FEWER cached entries — the (memory)/(entry_count) ratio is not roughly constant (03-23 implies a higher bytes-per-entry than the two earlier cycles).

TemplateCache grows monotonically in near-lockstep with the memory ramp within each of the three cycles and never evicts (evictions=0 on every line). 03-21: 51750->103500->155250->196650; 03-22: 51750->103500->155250->196650; 03-23: 49500->99000->148500->188100. The count resets only at the restart (03-23 21:00Z=9000 entries), mirroring the memory sawtooth, i.e. cache population and RSS rise together.

The 03-23 OOM-cycle old-gen WARN series ('heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took Nms', 10 events 18:34:46Z-19:49:28Z) and the 03-21/03-22 series (25 events) report only PERCENTAGE over a 90% threshold plus GC duration — no absolute old-gen bytes. So the only heap-side numbers available are '% over 90', entry counts, and memory_pct; none yields a byte attribution of live heap to TemplateCache vs other objects.

findings.statement: The cache is the only object whose growth is logged and does grow to ~200k entries while memory climbs to ~95% then resets exactly at restart, so TemplateCache is a large contributor consistent with H1; however because entry counts differ (188100 vs 196650) at comparable peak memory and no per-class byte data exists, this data can neither prove the cache holds a majority of live heap bytes nor exclude a co-resident non-cache leak (H5). The non-constant ratio is mild evidence that not all peak memory is cache-proportional.
